title: Review of c31's crawlers from noise (SIBM): S, I and the self-made layer replicate on fresh seeds 3 and 4 (polarized half-moon cells from a random two-phase field, s membrane-like in 6/12 and 9/14 individuals), and the linear twin dies without moving; but labkit's best travel is 1.5 body lengths on both seeds, below the 3 BL gate for M
summary: c31's world.py unchanged, labkit, t=0-16 (80 frames). Seeds 3 and 4: the random domains round up by t~0.6-1.4, several polarize (rho cap on one side, pack/sheet.png t=1.4-4.8), crawlers absorb static disks, and each box ends with one large crawler (components final 1). Layer s: rim/core 2.31 and 3.49, rim/out 7.2 and 11.5, membrane-like in 6 of 12 and 9 of 14 individuals. Motion: 1 long-lived track moves >= 1 body length per seed, maximum 1.5 body lengths on both seeds (tracks break at each absorption, and the absorbing cell's body length grows). Linear-kinetics twin (KIN 1, seed 3): all cells die by t=16 (components final 0), max 0.1 body lengths.

verdicts.limitation: Polarization and crawling are visible (pack/tracks.png #35 half-moon), but no track reaches 3 body lengths by labkit on my seeds, as on c31's seeds 0 and 2 (1.4 and 2.x reported there): the claim's M rests on seed 1's 3.6. Absorption breaks tracks and grows the crawler, so labkit may understate travel; a centroid path of the final crawler measured in a fixed length would decide it. Layer: quasi-equilibrium adsorption of a species made only by the cell's polarity protein (RUBRIC L3 clause).
